_about: The single source of truth for every mechanic term. codex is the rule as the player reads it; design.holes is what the mechanic does not do yet. docs/vocabulary.md is generated from this file by tools/export_vocabulary.gd. status: implemented (in sim/), planned (designed, not coded), idea (floated, undecided).

entries.name: Hull
entries.codex: Damage that gets past shield removes hull. Hull never recovers during a battle. At zero the machine is a wreck to be salvaged after the battle.

entries.name: HP
entries.codex: A foe's health. What gets past its armour takes HP off, and at zero the foe falls. A machine's health is its hull.

design.holes: A machine's health is its hull; the engine's code may say either word.

entries.name: Shield
entries.codex: Enemy damage hits shield before hull. A shield absorbs its number: a blow costs it its damage, and whatever it cannot absorb passes to the hull, armour coming off it there; a breaching blow ignores the shield, which stands, and the armour, so the whole blow reaches the hull. Shield components add shield up to the chassis maximum (a component with Overshield may pass it, and the excess fades at the end of the round); in a fight shield comes back from components, modules, passives and a chassis's shield regen. The shield is full as every fight opens, as the heat starts at zero; nothing returns on the map.

design.holes: Rates and shield sizes are placeholders. No in-combat trickle; a passive may bring one back for one chassis.

entries.name: Heat
entries.codex: A component that prints heat adds it when spent. At the end of your turn, before the enemy acts, heat above the chassis maximum burns hull one for one and the gauge settles at the maximum; until then a vent can still bring it down, and a machine the burn wrecks is lost on its own turn. Vent components remove heat. At the start of every round a machine sheds its chassis's cooling rating in heat, so a round spent on shields or cool weapons is a way of cooling down without a vent. Foes never add heat outright: a Burning machine gains its heat at the end of your turn, just before the overheat, and a Scorched machine's weapons and equipment aimed at foes run hotter.

design.holes: Heat does nothing below the cap. Consider effects at high heat short of overflow. Cooling numbers are placeholders; cooling must stay below a typical weapon's heat or heat never matters, and a vent component must be worth a whole turn (tuning).

entries.name: Reroll
entries.codex: Two rerolls per round, each rerolling every unlocked, unspent die. A reroll lands on any other component on the die, never the one showing; a second copy of the same component may come up. Rerolls may be spent before or after attacking, so a low damage roll is information for the rest of the round. Never pooled across rounds, unless a Giant Petrel fights: its Maverick's Playbook banks up to three left unspent as your turn ends, for the next round.

entries.name: Rift Pressure
entries.codex: Ticks once per battlefield phase, never inside a fight. It fills at the ramp's beat (3 turns, 2 from Convergence 8), a turn short of its peak as a battle opens, and the beat halves once at the Rupture. When full it resets and peaks: the rift sends the next composition of its cycle, every tear open before the peak sends a patrol, the seam creeps toward the gate, and new tears open on it. It never stops: the boss's seal breaking does not quiet it.

design.holes: The interval step inside a battle (the escalation a stall would meet) is on the ramp's table at zero until the turtle read asks for it.

entries.name: Rupture meter
entries.codex: Fills by the menace of the foes you kill, in any fight however it ends, toward the tier's Fractures (three, four or five). The Fractures are set from the field's menace at the start and the first compositions the rift will send, the last at two thirds of it and each later one costing more. The last Fracture is the Rupture: the boss's seal breaks. It also breaks once nothing but the boss's pack stands as a fight ends.

design.holes: Shown as a bar under the gate's with a notch a Fracture, a first cut; the share and the steps are placeholders.

entries.name: Fracture
entries.codex: A step of the Rupture meter, paid out as a fight ends. At the Fractures the tier names (tier one's first; tier two's first and third; tier three's first, second and fourth) an elite emerges at the rift, the lead domain's elites in turn and never twice in a battle. The last Fracture is the Rupture.

design.holes: The prize a Fracture may bring is not built (decided after the meter is played); the Peak has no elite yet, so its Fractures send none.

entries.name: Gate Integrity
entries.codex: Each pusher makes for a segment of the wall of its own, drawn as it is dealt. A pusher that ends its walk beside any hex of the gate or the wall strikes the gate's bar for a third of its strength, at least one. The whole wall is the target, so no line plugs it. Gate integrity persists across battles and is repaired in the meta.

design.holes: The gate damage formula is a placeholder; city defences along the wall are not built.

entries.name: Weapon
entries.codex: A component that deals damage: spent on a foe within its reach, it deals its number in damage, then its keywords act and its heat lands. One that deals none is equipment. A passive may make another kind a weapon on its machine too (the Whip Scorpion's vents): its hold reads both, Vent, Weapon.

design.holes: The engine's kind is attack for a weapon and a debuff alike: a debuff is an attack of no damage (Face.is_debuff), so code asks is_weapon() for this word and is_attack() for both.

entries.name: Shield component
entries.codex: Spend on self or an ally to add its power in shield, capped at that machine's shield maximum.

entries.name: Vent component
entries.codex: Spend on self or an ally to remove its power in heat.

entries.name: Equipment
entries.codex: A buff or a debuff: a component that deals no damage. A buff is spent on a machine (itself, an ally, or either, as it says) and grants it a status; a debuff is spent on a foe within its reach, its keywords its whole effect. Shields and vents are kinds of their own.

entries.name: Buff component
entries.codex: Equipment spent on a machine (itself, an ally, or either, as the component says) that grants it a status, so many stacks deep, through the end of so many rounds: Empowered for damage, Armoured against damage, Primed to burn on hit. A status that runs down on its own (Empowered, halving) takes no rounds. The die shows the status name and the stacks.

entries.name: Direct
entries.codex: Targets any front-rank foe, and any back-rank foe whose column is exposed.

entries.name: Indirect
entries.codex: Targets any foe in either rank, at no cost to its firer.

entries.name: Spread
entries.codex: Keyword with a number. Spread 2 also hits the foes beside the target in its rank, each taking 2 where the target takes the number: the attacker's bonuses land on that 2 as on the blow, then each foe's own statuses and armour. On a debuff it carries no number: its effects reach those foes, and it deals nothing.

design.holes: Its number rides on the entry beside the keyword (cleave), and the validator asks for it on a weapon. The half it dealt from 26 October retired 28 October (Ryan): at single digits a neighbour's half killed no rank and file.

entries.name: Penetrate
entries.codex: Keyword with a number. Penetrate 3 also hits the other rank of the target's column, which takes 3 where the target takes the number: the attacker's bonuses land on that 3 as on the blow, then the foe's own statuses and armour. A massive foe fills its column, so it is hit once. On a debuff it carries no number.

design.holes: Its number rides on the entry beside the keyword (penetrate), and the validator asks for it on a weapon.

entries.name: Splash
entries.codex: Keyword with a number. Splash 1 also hits every foe round the target, those beside it in its rank and the other rank of its column, each taking 1 where the target takes the number: the attacker's bonuses land on that 1 as on the blow, then each foe's own statuses and armour. On a debuff it carries no number.

design.holes: Spread and Penetrate at one number, one chip on the die (Ryan, 28 October: Splash N back 'for the sake of display simplicity'); the validator refuses the two at one number and Splash beside either. Its number rides on the entry (splash).

entries.name: Every Foe
entries.codex: Targeting mode, a debuff's. Dropped on any foe, the entry lands on every foe in the fight, front rank and back, as it lands on its target. A Silence leaves it whole: it mutes keywords, never a targeting mode.

design.holes: A keyword from 2 November (Ryan: 'Every foe is a targeting mode, just like spread, penetrate, and splash, it should be listed as such and given a keyword'), a targeting mode in its own right since 4 November ('Silence should not narrow targeting modes, that's why I'm switching them to targeting modes'), drawn in the die's targeting slot. A working name, the foes' Every Machine mirrored. A weapon's area is Spread, Penetrate or Splash with its number, so the validator holds Every Foe to a debuff (the Heliographic Siphon's lure-all) until a damaging one is designed.

entries.name: Every Ally
entries.codex: Targeting mode, a shield's or a buff's. Spent on any machine, the entry lands on the whole team, its own machine among them, each taking all of it. A Silence leaves it whole: it mutes keywords, never a targeting mode.

design.holes: Every Foe's mirror on the team's side (2 November; a targeting mode since 4 November); a working name. Its mark is the three hexes under a low arch, its own cell lit (Ryan, 4 November: 'the difference is whether the center one is lit or not, its two modes, even if the every ally doesn't actually exist in game, yet'): no piece carries it yet. Never a vent's (the validator).

entries.name: Every Other Ally
entries.codex: Targeting mode, a shield's or a buff's. Spent on an ally, the entry lands on every machine but its own, each taking all of it. A Silence leaves it whole: it mutes keywords, never a targeting mode.

design.holes: Every Ally's other mode (4 November), the Mooring Screens' team shield; a working name. Its mark is Every Ally's with its own cell dark. Never a vent's (the validator).

entries.name: Spillover
entries.codex: The Wild Boar's rule, granted to every weapon it fires by its Juggernaut Drive and run by the engine as a keyword: when a blow kills a front-rank foe, what it had past the kill carries into the foe behind it in the same column. Nothing stands behind a massive foe. No component carries it; it becomes a keyword the player learns on its own if a second source ever grants it.

design.holes: The spill is plain damage: it spends a Shock and feeds the Ammit's kill rule, and carries no other keyword of the blow.

entries.name: Cryo
entries.codex: Keyword with a number. Every foe the entry reaches gains that many stacks of Cryo a strike (Cryo 1: one stack), laid once the strikes are done, so a fire never cashes its own frost. Any machine's hit with a weapon on a foe carrying Cryo spends every stack and cools the hitter 2 a stack.

design.holes: Other pieces may lay it (marked for reuse as a healthier ally cooling than a vent). A rider on the mark is benched until the roster has room. The cooling a stack is a placeholder.

entries.name: Burn
entries.codex: Keyword with a number. On a player's weapon or equipment, Burn 3 means each foe hit gains three stacks of Burning. On a foe's attack the same: each blow that lands leaves that many stacks of Burning on the machine it hit.

design.holes: Its number rides on the face beside the keyword (burn), and the validator asks for it.

entries.name: Lure
entries.codex: Player keyword, on any entry aimed at a foe, a weapon or equipment. Every foe the entry reaches turns on this machine for the round, a felled one too, intents and all; reach and area decide who and how many. A lured foe whose move has no target keeps doing it.

design.holes: No status and no chip: the arrow is the record. A draw by an ally is parked (the bible's redirection row).

entries.name: Shock
entries.codex: Player keyword, on any entry aimed at a foe. Every foe the entry reaches is Shocked, a felled one too: the next weapon strike aimed at it deals double. The entry's own blow never spends the shock it leaves.

entries.name: Expose
entries.codex: Player keyword, on any entry aimed at a foe. Every foe the entry reaches is Exposed through the next round, a felled one too: in Direct reach of every machine, and its armour counts for nothing. A second Expose refreshes it, never adds.

design.holes: The formation word exposed stays rules text, so the status's id is exposure.

entries.name: Disrupt
entries.codex: Player keyword, on any entry aimed at a foe. The foe does its other move instead, this round, and its new intent shows at once. A foe with nothing else open is not moved, and a follow-up it announced is not either: the move it came after was the window.

design.holes: Deterministic: the next move in the foe's list that its conditions allow, so a boss steps through its pattern.

entries.name: Suppress
entries.codex: Player keyword. The target skips its telegraphed action this round, and recovers with its stun resist in Numbed. On a Numbed foe the stun strips a stack and lands nothing; a Ward turns it away.

entries.name: Web
entries.codex: The funnel-web's Web Bomb, locked: the foe hit is Webbed, no damage. After its action the web bursts, Suppressing it and the next foe to act beside it.

design.holes: A keyword, so its chip and checks come free; the burst runs at the end of the foe's action (Skirmish._web_burst).

entries.name: Swap
entries.codex: Player keyword, the Dingo's Combat Translocator's: the spend takes two targets, a foe and then another foe or an empty slot, and the two trade places; no damage. A massive foe does not move. Drag the die to the first, drop it, then tap the second; drag it again to move it, or tap the ground to set it back.

entries.name: Flak
entries.codex: Flak N: each foe hit gains N stacks of Flak a strike, laid once the strikes are done, so no strike of the spend feeds on what it lays.

design.holes: The stacks land after the blow, so the blow that lays them never feeds on them and a later strike of the same spend does.

entries.name: Numbed
entries.codex: Foe buff: the rounds until one stun lands. A stun on it strips a stack and lands nothing, so a foe with Numbed N takes N+1 stuns in a round. A stunned foe recovers with its stun resist in stacks (1 for most, 2 for a massive foe, 3 for an elite, a hero or a boss), after the round's decay; a stack goes at the end of each round. A Purge lowers it like any buff; nothing deepens, spreads or cleanses it.

design.holes: Ryan's clock (2 November): the chip reads as the rounds until it can be stunned again, so the stacks land after the decay phase; a stun lock costs its resist and one every round, so an all-in stun team can brute-force a boss at a price, and a Purge is the other key. The resist numbers are placeholders (content's resist; the bosses' by hand).

table.stacks: Yes: its stun resist as it recovers from a stun
table.lasts: A stack goes at the end of each round

entries.name: Paradox
entries.codex: Foe status. While a machine runs the Paradox meter (the Baboon's Pocket Paradox), a foe gains a stack each time it gains any other status: one a spend, however many strikes or stacks. At the machine's count (three) its past self knocks it out: it is Suppressed and the Paradox clears. A foe already suppressed loses its next action instead. Never decays. A status like any other: it counts for what reads a status, and a machine that deepens the statuses it applies deepens it.

design.holes: The count is a placeholder.

table.stacks: Yes: one a debuff gained, a spend; at three it Suppresses and clears
table.lasts: The skirmish; never decays

entries.name: Volatile
entries.codex: A cost printed on any kind of component, along its foot beside its heat, the hull's mark (a machine's body) and a number. Volatile 3 means spending it costs its owner 3 hull, past shield and armour, before the component acts, and a machine it leaves at nothing is wrecked. A blank is never spent, so a disabled entry costs nothing.

design.holes: Hull outright, where the Corrupted bite takes shield first. The number is a placeholder. A keyword with a chip until 26 October; a cost like heat since, so the die says the price and no chip does.

entries.name: Shield cost
entries.codex: A cost printed on any kind of component, along its foot beside its heat, the shield's mark and a number: spending it takes that much shield from its owner first, overshield included. Short of it, the entry cannot be played: the die shows the cost struck through, and it has nowhere to land.

design.fantasy: Ryan, 26 October: a price paid in the buffer, which overshield cheats out at the cost of two actions for one effect; the first entry with a condition on its play, so advanced pieces may follow.
design.holes: No piece carries it yet; the numbers are content's.

entries.name: Empowered a kill
entries.codex: A rule printed on a weapon (the Soulcutter Talons', locked on the Ammit), with no word of its own: every foe it kills gives its owner a stack of Empowered, which the Ammit keeps for the battle.

design.holes: A spread that kills two feeds twice; a chain feeds on every link.

entries.name: Targets
entries.codex: Whom a shield, a vent or a buff may be spent on: any ally or itself (the default), itself only, any other ally, or every machine at once: the whole team (Every Ally) or every machine but its own (Every Other Ally). On the die three connected hexes stand under its main mark, the middle its own machine and the two beside it its allies, a filled one a machine it may be spent on: all three for either, the middle alone for itself only, the two beside it for allies only.

entries.name: Chain
entries.codex: Keyword with a number, a weapon's. Chain 2 also lands 2 on every other Shocked foe on the field, wherever it stands, where the target takes the number: the attacker's bonuses land on that 2 as on the blow, then each foe's own statuses and armour. No strike is aimed at them, so their Shock stands.

design.holes: Shock's other payoff (Ryan, 28 October: 'the thinking man's AoE'); the kill and repeat and the ping retired; 29 October, Ryan's pick from six looks measured that day: its arcs plain and never spending a charge, with Shock read by a weapon's strike aimed at the foe alone, and a random charge after the arcs, since the arc was short of charges to find. Its number rides on the entry (chain). Retired 3 November: the charge, one other foe at random after the arcs (Ryan, 2 November: "Chain just is the situational aoe, and if weak we can either add more things for it to proc on, or give it the self-charge again"); Charged, the primer, supplies the Shock beside the Shock weapons and Retaliate.

entries.name: Rapid
entries.codex: After this component is spent the machine acts again: the die rerolls for free onto any other component (a second copy of this one included, so copies chain). The Cassowary's Spin-Up spins the whole die instead, itself included, the one Rapid that may land on itself. Rapid carries no cooldown of its own: a Rapid component prints its cooldown, a cost the die shows by its clock, or pays heat or hull every spend instead. Any component may carry it, a vent or a shield as well as a weapon.

design.holes: Every Rapid piece carries a limiter (a cooldown, heat or Volatile), which the validator holds content to; a Rapid vent is never below tier three and a Rapid shield never below tier two (the bible's Rapid row).

entries.name: Disable
entries.codex: Enemy keyword. The component the target's die is showing is switched off through the target's next turn: if the die lands on it, it comes up blank.

entries.name: Steal
entries.codex: Enemy keyword. The component the target's die is showing is switched off through the target's next turn, as a Disable, and the foe takes it: its next swing lands that weapon's number, and anything that was no weapon is a fake, for 1. A Ward turns it away.

design.holes: Gilgamesh's (30 October). One piece held at a time, the swing spending it; the swing is one strike at the piece's number, whatever strikes the piece had, and no keyword of the piece rides it.

entries.name: Drain
entries.codex: Enemy keyword. The foe regrows what the blow took from the hull, no more than the machine had, so a shield starves it. It lays nothing on the machine, so no Ward turns it away; a Barrier's blow deals nothing to drain, and Burning on the foe takes back what it heals.

design.holes: The Vampire Lord's (30 October), its bite and, below half, a drain at every machine. The genre's word (Drain), and the soft counter section 2 asks for: burn never stops healing. The hull alone, so the shield answers it: a drain of shield and hull walled the slowest trio at every HP tried, the shield, its answer to every blow, doing nothing against the heal.

entries.name: Corrupt
entries.codex: Foe attack keyword with a number. Each blow that lands leaves that many stacks of Corrupted on the component the target's die is showing (Corrupt 2: two): it deals damage to its owner whenever spent, a bite a stack.

entries.name: Silence
entries.codex: Foe move of its own, never a rider on a blow. The machine it lands on is Silenced: its components' keywords are muted through its next round, printed and granted alike; its buffs count and its stores fill as ever. A Ward turns it away.

design.holes: Who carries it is section 12's question. It mutes the machine's keywords and never its buffs (Ryan, 27 and 28 October); cast with no condition, aimed as its move says.

entries.name: Swallow
entries.codex: Foe move of its own, never a rider on a blow. The machine it lands on is Swallowed: out of the fight for the rounds it says, until the swallower falls, or until the swallower has lost a quarter of its HP since the swallow, the damage still to deal counting down on its chip. It never takes the last machine able to act. A Ward turns it away; a Lure turns it, and a Suppress or a Disrupt stops it, as any move.

design.holes: Floraison's (30 October). The rounds, 1 to 3, are the move's, and no damage lands on the machine while it is held. The early release (31 October, Ryan agreeing Claude's lean): a quarter of the swallower's HP lost since the swallow, Clair Obscur's stagger in its smallest form, a round of the team's focus; the swallower loses nothing else, since a lost action on top would be a stun. A machine let go in the player's turn acts that round.

entries.name: Golden Rage
entries.codex: Foe move of its own, never a rider on a blow: the foe goes gold (Golden) for the rounds it says, so the round it roars is the window to shield up or to start the burst. It goes gold only while calm, so one rage at a time; a Suppress or a Disrupt stops the roar, as any move.

design.holes: The Thunder Ape's (4 November); see Golden. Its weight is content's, 2 so it comes about a round in three while calm.

entries.name: Merge
entries.codex: Foe move of its own. Every other foe on the field of the kinds it names is taken into it, gone without falling: it regrows the HP they had left, and its next move hits harder for each one. Thin them first; a Suppress or a Disrupt stops it, as any move.

design.holes: The King Gel's (30 October): every Gel, Bubble Gel, Metal Gel and half on the field. Content: effect merge, foe (an id or a list), value (the lift a foe taken in). A foe taken in leaves no last act and no split and is no kill of the team's; its pack's tally still counts it gone. It needs its kinds beside it, so the King Gel's escort is its own (an escort that names its boss).

entries.name: Purge
entries.codex: Purge N, on either side. On a player's entry aimed at a foe, a weapon or equipment, every foe it reaches loses N stacks of every buff it carries (an unstackable one is a stack of one), after the blow, so a foe the blow kills stays down. On a foe's move of its own, never a rider on a blow and never a last act's, the machine it lands on loses N stacks of every buff it carries, for good. A stack is a stack, whatever granted it; an Ability is no buff and stays, and so do the stores and a stack its passive keeps. A Ward turns it away and stands, on either side.

design.holes: One id, dispel, on both sides, as breach is (28 October); numbered 2 November (Ryan: "lower everything by N and price accordingly", a softer answer to armour and damage stacking that prices cheap and common; the Null Field Emitter at Purge 2, a placeholder). One purge on either side (Effects.purge): N stacks off every buff, whatever granted it (Ryan, 8 November: "A stack is a stack, doesn't matter where it came from"); retired with it the purge by source of 28 October (a die entry's stacks gone for good, a store's, a form's or a passive's put to sleep until the player's turn), which he called cryptic. What the unit is, its form or its passive mechanic, is an Ability and no buff, so no purge reaches it (the same day).

entries.name: Cleanse
entries.codex: Player keyword, on shield and vent components. Whoever the component is spent on also loses every Burning, Scorched, Crushed, Silenced, Disabled and Corrupted status. A rapid component's own switch-off is not a status a cleanse touches. On a foe's move of its own, the same word: every mark the team laid (Burning, Flak, Cryo, Vitriol, Shocked, Exposed, Webbed, the Paradox, the Drone) comes off the most-marked of its own, never Numbed or Suppressed.

entries.name: Overshield
entries.codex: Player keyword, on shield components, rare. The shield may raise its target past the target's maximum; shield past the maximum fades at the end of the round, or as the fight ends. A shield die spent on a machine already at its maximum is never wasted when it carries this.

design.holes: Rare because every overshield on the field makes shield max a soft number; the fade is the whole safeguard, since a lasting excess would stack a team past every blow.

entries.name: Retaliate
entries.codex: Machine status. While it lasts, a foe that strikes this machine's bare hull is Shocked. It lasts the rounds the component that grants it says.

table.stacks: No: one does all it does
table.lasts: The buff's rounds

entries.name: Shocked
entries.codex: Foe status. When a weapon's strike aimed at this foe lands, it deals double damage and the status clears. A blow that only reaches it (an area, a Chain's arc, a spill) neither doubles nor clears it, and equipment (a lure, a probe) leaves it standing. Never stacks. Laid by the Shock keyword, by a Charged machine's weapon, and on a foe that strikes the bare hull of a machine carrying Retaliate.

table.stacks: Never
table.lasts: Until the next team blow of a weapon

entries.name: Exposed
entries.codex: Foe status. In Direct reach of every machine as if its column's front were empty, and its armour counts for nothing, its own and any Armoured. Through the next round; refreshed, never added.

design.holes: The id is exposure, since exposed names the formation word and the foes' default aim.

table.stacks: Never: a second Expose refreshes it
table.lasts: Through the next round

entries.name: Empowered
entries.codex: Machine status. Each stack is +1 damage on this machine's attacks, flat, so the count is the bonus. At the end of each round it halves, rounded down, whatever granted it, until it is gone. On the Ammit nothing of it fades: its Quintessence Tap keeps every stack for the battle.

design.holes: Every grant is one status on the machine and the stacks add up. A halving rule has no duration, so a buff component grants stacks and no rounds. The name is a placeholder.

table.stacks: Yes: a damage point a stack
table.lasts: Halves at the end of each round, rounded down, until gone; on the Ammit the battle, nothing fading

entries.name: Sealed
entries.codex: Ability, the Polar Bear's form. A shield it spends on itself seals it: armour up by its Lockdown's number, its own cooling stopped, its Cryo Flinger gaining Spread, and it runs hotter at the end of each turn. A vent or a weapon opens it; a shield on an ally and equipment leave it as it is; an entry that cools and shields at once does the one its form calls for. An ally's vent still cools it. No Purge touches it.

design.holes: One chip, renewing, never stacking: the armour it grants is tied to the form. The numbers are placeholders.

table.stacks: Renews: one seal however many shields
table.lasts: Until a vent or a weapon opens it, or the skirmish ends

entries.name: Cryo
entries.codex: Foe status, the mark the Cryo keyword leaves. Any machine's hit on it with a weapon spends every stack and cools the hitter 2 a stack; equipment spends none. It never fades on its own.

design.holes: Engine id cryoed, since the keyword holds cryo; the player reads Cryo on both.

table.stacks: Yes: the Cryo's number per foe reached; a weapon's hit spends every stack
table.lasts: Until a weapon's hit spends it, or the skirmish ends

entries.name: Armoured
entries.codex: Status, on either side. Armour +1 a stack: that much off every blow that reaches it, flat, every stack at once, whatever granted it, so the count is the armour. On a machine (a buff, an armouring component, a passive) it lasts until the round's end and comes off blows on bare hull; on a foe, from its brace, it lasts until its next action.

design.holes: The engine id stays braced.

table.stacks: Yes: an armour point a stack, every stack going at once
table.lasts: A machine's until the round's end; a foe's until its next action

entries.name: Primed
entries.codex: Status, on either side. Every blow it lands leaves a stack of Burning per stack of Primed. On a machine, a buff grants it for the rounds it says. On a foe, a stoker's move primes every other foe on the field at its value, and its next move spends it, whatever it is: a foe acting after the stoker spends it this turn, one that has acted carries it to its next move. A machine's Ward turns its Burning away, as it does any rider.

design.holes: A placeholder name.

table.stacks: Yes: a Burning stack a blow per stack
table.lasts: A machine's the buff's rounds; a foe's its next move

entries.name: Disabled
entries.codex: Component status. This die entry comes up blank while it lasts; the component itself is untouched. A foe's disable lasts through the machine's next turn and can be cleansed; a rapid component's own switch-off ends with the round.

table.stacks: No
table.lasts: Through the machine's next turn

entries.name: Corrupted
entries.codex: Component status. Every time this die entry is spent it bites its owner for 3 per stack, shield first, before the component acts. A blank is never spent, so a disabled entry does not bite. Stacks. Clears at end of skirmish. Can be cleansed.

design.holes: The bite is the status's own number in the engine's table, a placeholder.

table.stacks: Yes: its bite a stack
table.lasts: The skirmish

entries.name: Crushed
entries.codex: Machine status, from a foe's crush (the World Eater's pin): every blow it takes deals a point more a stack, the shield taking the extra first as it takes any blow, through the next round, when every stack goes. A Ward turns the crush away; an ally's Cleanse lifts it.

design.holes: Monster Hunter's Defense Down by archetype, the pin's mark (Ryan, 4 November: rework the World Eater's below-half bite "into a form of its pin, since that inflicts Defense Down in game, something we don't have"). Claude's form: Flak's shape on the other body, a point a blow a stack, so every machine feels it and the chip is a number; the forms not taken, its armour counting for nothing through the round (nothing on a car) and its shield halved (fiddly at single digits). Numbers placeholders.

table.stacks: Yes: a point more a blow a stack
table.lasts: Through the next round, every stack at once

entries.name: Phased
entries.codex: Machine status. It cannot act, take damage or be targeted until the round's end: a blow or a move at every machine passes it by. Granted only to a machine that has not acted this round.

design.holes: Not targetable means allies cannot vent or shield it either, and a foe's intent on it picks again; it still cools by its own cooling, and ticks and overheats still land. Aphelion's pieces may grant it beside the Swallowtail's screens.

table.stacks: No
table.lasts: Until the round's end

entries.name: Burning
entries.codex: Status. On a foe: loses 1 HP per stack at the start of its action, then loses one stack; bypasses armour. On a machine: gains 1 heat per stack at the end of the player's turn, before the overheat, then loses one stack, so a vent makes room for it or a cleanse takes it off. Metal does not burn, it heats.

design.holes: Engine ids burning (a foe's) and burning_mech (a machine's).

table.stacks: Yes: the Burn's number per blow, or as many as the foe's move says
table.lasts: Until the stacks run out: one fades at each tick (a foe's action; the end of the player's turn on a machine)

entries.name: Suppressed
entries.codex: Foe status. Skips its action this round, then clears.

table.stacks: No
table.lasts: One action: this round's, or the next if it has acted

entries.name: Vitriol
entries.codex: Foe status, the funnel-web's acid. At its action it loses 10% of its current HP a stack, past armour, after Burning, rounded down, then a stack fades. A share of what is left: it opens on a boss and never finishes a foe.

design.holes: Only the funnel-web's passive lays it; a keyword that ever carries it shares the word. Whether a tick passes Guarded is the parts' question, as Burning's is. The word Corroded is kept for a foe's damage over time on machines.

table.stacks: Yes: a stack per weapon hit on a foe showing no intent on the spider; a tick a stack
table.lasts: A stack fades at each of its actions

entries.name: Webbed
entries.codex: Foe status, the funnel-web's web. At the end of its action the web bursts: it and the next foe to act beside it are Suppressed, each a stun like any other (a Numbed foe strips a stack instead, a Warded one turns it). Killed first, it takes its web with it; one the team has already suppressed gains nothing from the burst on itself.

design.holes: The burst catches the next foe to act beside it in its rank, the one to its left when none stands to its right; on a foe already suppressed it is wasted, and each half feeds the Paradox as the Suppress keyword's does.

table.stacks: No
table.lasts: Until the end of its action this round, when it bursts

entries.name: Spun Up
entries.codex: Machine status, the Cassowary's. The next weapon it spends deals 2 more a stack and takes every stack; equipment leaves them standing. Carried between turns until then.

design.holes: Spent whole by the next weapon, equipment leaving it: weapon only until balance says otherwise (Ryan, 26 October).

table.stacks: Yes: its bonus a stack, every stack spent by the next weapon
table.lasts: Until the next weapon it spends, across turns

entries.name: Hot Streak
entries.codex: Ability, the Kite's: its shots run 1 hotter a stack this fight, a stack for each attack that killed. Its passive's price: no cleanse, silence or purge lifts it.

design.holes: A working name, the Kite's heat tax.

table.stacks: Yes: one for each attack that killed
table.lasts: The fight

entries.name: Shots
entries.codex: Machine count, the Cassowary's: every weapon and equipment it aims at a foe this fight, shown as six pips under the heat bar, the sixth lit when it is next, where its sixth shot counts double. Shields, vents, buffs and spins are no shots. Never a chip; nothing cleanses it; it resets each fight.

design.holes: Kept only for a machine whose rule counts (an nth_shot condition).

table.stacks: Yes: one a weapon or equipment aimed at a foe
table.lasts: The skirmish; never decays

entries.name: Quick turn spent
entries.codex: Machine marker, the Needletail's gate: its free setup this round is spent, so its next debuff or buff this round is a full action. Never a chip: the die shows the gate open by the Rapid it grants a setup. Gone at the round's end.

design.holes: Set by a static grant of Rapid on setup_once (the Needletail's relay).

table.stacks: No
table.lasts: The round

entries.name: Siphoning
entries.codex: Machine status, the Whip Scorpion's Siphon: every blow a foe lands on it this round adds heat, 2 a blow, whatever the blow dealt. The blows land in the enemy's turn, after the overheat, so it is next round's fuel for its vents, or next turn's burn. Until the round's end; nothing cleanses it.

design.holes: The number is the entry's own (heat_per_blow), the lever.

table.stacks: No: its entry's heat a blow
table.lasts: Until the round's end

entries.name: Flak
entries.codex: Foe status, Wainwright & Sutler's on-hit. Every blow of a weapon it takes deals a point more a stack. At the end of each round the stacks halve, rounded down.

design.holes: Adds before multiplies and before armour, to a weapon's blow of 0 too (Ryan, 25 October: "Flak and overcharge exist in part to get past armour"), so a Shocked foe carrying Flak takes blow plus Flak, doubled. The id follows the participle habit (Burning, Webbed). Numbers are placeholders; Flak beside Empowered at a point a stack each may read too strong, the two read together on the Prairie Dog's rows.

table.stacks: Yes: N a hit from a Flak N piece; a point more on every blow of a weapon it takes, a stack
table.lasts: Halves at the end of each round, rounded down, until gone

entries.name: Destroyed component
entries.codex: Machine status, global rule. When what one blow puts on the hull, past shield and armour, is at least a quarter of its maximum hull, the entry the die shows is destroyed: blank, it does nothing when it comes up, and provides its passive bonuses but not passive abilities, for the rest of the battle; after it, a hardpoint's is gone for good and a built-in one is rebuilt. A shield prevents it only by absorbing enough of the blow, and a blow a Barrier takes never injures. An injury that lands on a destroyed component or an empty hardpoint finds nothing to break, so a machine showing a broken entry shrugs it off, and what faces the enemy is the player's choice.

design.holes: The threshold is a placeholder, set by what it asks of the player, never by a loss or win rate (Ryan, 25 October). The campaign's hangar screen is not built.

entries.name: Front rank
entries.codex: Four slots, one a column. Front-rank foes fill these. Always in Direct reach.

entries.name: Back rank
entries.codex: Four slots behind the front. Back-rank foes hold these.

entries.name: Mine
entries.codex: Foe status, the Lammergeier's: every weapon and equipment it aims at a foe adds its flat damage to a Mine on that foe, with what the spend fired at it: every hit's stacks and its other keywords, one Mine a foe however many spends feed it. When the foe falls, even one that gets back up or splits, the Mine blows: its damage on every foe round its slot, each through its own Flak and armour (none under Breach), then its keywords as on a blow. Spread, Penetrate, Splash, Spillover, Sweep's targeting and Lure stay with the spend, and its damage never grows with the spend's. The chip shows its damage; its readout, its keywords.

design.holes: Ryan, 9 November: "the lammergeier basically converts all hits to AoE hits, at the cost of a delay until Death". One Mine a spend at a flat 2 ("then look at per hit later if it's weak"); its riders the spend's whole result on the foe ("the mine should take the entire result of the spend, then apply it. So a 3-hit flak that burns 1 per hit if the target is under 50% HP, would result in adding a 2 damage mine with 3 flak, and 0-3 burn"), every hit's stacks as its machine deepened and doubled them and a gated keyword where its gate held ("if a gate is met when fired only, then apply it"); the numbered ones add up and the rest ride once; Chain rides as its arcs (Claude's lean, which he took); in the enemy's turn a Mine's Disrupt does nothing; a Suppress rides as fired, each foe the blast meets judging its own Numbed (Claude's read; Ryan: "Your reads are correct"). A mark the team laid: a Ward turns it away, a foe's cleanse takes it, the Paradox counts it. A foe taken into a merge hands its Mine to the merger.

table.stacks: Yes: its damage, every spend adding to it, one Mine a foe
table.lasts: The fight, until the foe falls or the Syrinx Drone detonates it

entries.name: Massive
entries.codex: A massive foe fills both slots of a column and counts as front rank. Its column is never exposed while it stands. Only some elites and bosses are massive.

design.holes: Spread treats it as a front-rank neighbour; Penetrate finds nothing behind it.

entries.name: Movespeed
entries.codex: Move in hexes: how far a machine goes in an action, a step a hex. Water costs a ground machine two; a hovercraft and a flyer cross it at one; walls are the flyer's alone.

design.holes: Every chassis's move is a placeholder set by size and role; what crossing water and walls is worth is the pricing run's to read (28 October).

entries.name: Walk
entries.codex: The map shows where every pack will walk on the enemy's turn, worked out from where your machines stand now: a pusher toward the gate, a hunter toward its prey. Packs go round your machines; nothing you do stops one, and nothing a pack does reacts to your plan.

design.holes: A pack with no way to the gate waits, and the map says so.

entries.name: Fight
entries.codex: Tap a pack to attack it. One pack is one fight: nothing joins it, and you commit the machines beside it. Orders onto several packs play one fight at a time, each resolved before the next and fought to its end; a machine that fought, won or lost, is spent until your next turn.

entries.name: Spent
entries.codex: A machine that has fought this turn is spent: it cannot move or fight again until your next turn. A machine whose passive grants a second action has two before it is spent.

entries.name: Carry
entries.codex: A machine that carries (the Swallowtail's Muster Deck) lifts the machines on the hexes beside it when it moves: they travel as a ring round it and land as a block, each where it rode from it, keeping whatever move and action they had. It cannot stop where a rider would land on a hex it cannot stand on (NO ROOM). A caught machine does not ride.

design.holes: A landing animation or a redistribution on landing may come later.

entries.name: Caught
entries.codex: A machine a hunter has caught fights it first on your turn, before any other fight, and cannot move until then. Others in range may join that fight. It is fought to its end: the hunter falls or the machine is wrecked.

entries.name: Ring
entries.codex: A hunter catches what stands beside where its walk ends: the engage range, one hex, the same reach every unit has on the map, so a machine joins a fight on a pack beside it and a hunter catches a machine beside it. The map draws the ring of hexes beside the hunter's walk's end, where the catch is judged, and round the hunter while a catch it made waits. No other pack has a ring. No pack joins a fight; one pack is one fight.

design.holes: One number in the engine, the engage range (Unit.ENGAGE_RANGE, a placeholder: adjacency), serving the machines' reach onto a pack, the hunters' catch and the ring drawn; the hunters' pounce of two (Ryan, 29 October, "wolfs pounce") retired 10 November with the body blocking, so the catch is "the same melee engage range as everyone else" (Ryan); no foe or composition carries a ring since 8 November.

entries.name: Behaviour
entries.codex: A pack pushes unless its composition hunts. A pusher walks toward the gate and threatens nothing else. A hunter locks one machine, by its caveat (the nearest, weakest, strongest or slowest), puts its tag on it and walks toward it; when it ends its walk beside its prey it has caught it, and that fight comes first on your next turn. A caught machine cannot move until the fight, and is caught again while the hunter lives. A prey that keeps its distance is safe; one sealed off behind walls and machines is not: the hunter catches whichever machine it can reach that turn standing nearest it, and its tag moves there.

design.holes: Push and hunt are the only behaviours; the hunters' caveats are placeholders.

entries.name: Pack
entries.codex: An enemy hex is a pack: a composition on one hex, its members listed on a hold, wearing its lead's picture, hunting when its composition says so, walking at its slowest member's pace. Its hold says first how many machines it is a fight for, its threat rating; a pusher walks to a segment of the wall of its own. A fight is the one pack you attack. A boss is one unit on one hex.

entries.name: Footprint
entries.codex: Every unit covers one hex, the boss included: it is occupied, counts for rings and range, and is a tap target. The gate and the rift are wider structures.

design.holes: Footprints do not rotate with facing.

entries.name: Structure
entries.codex: Gate and rift hexes are structures wider than one hex. Nobody stands on them. A pack that ends its walk beside a gate hex or a wall hex strikes the gate. A tear is a mouth, not a structure: its hex can be walked and stood on.

entries.name: Spawn
entries.codex: At a peak of Rift Pressure the next composition of the rift's cycle (the tier's formations and patrols in turn, the lead domain's and the guest's in turn) emerges at the rift, and every tear open before the peak sends a patrol. A spawn lands on the nearest free hex to its mouth with no machine beside it, at the end of the enemy's turn, so you see it and its walk for a whole turn and nothing lands on top of a detachment.

entries.name: Composition
entries.codex: What the rift sends and what stands on the field when a battle starts: a patrol (a few foes, one machine's fight), a formation (the body's fight), an elite leading its own, or a boss's escort. A composition is one pack on one hex: its members, listed on a hold, unpack into the fight together and come back by member. Each domain writes its compositions by tier; the ramp sets how many stand at the start and how thick they are.

design.holes: Each tier's compositions are partitioned from its list as placeholders for Ryan's marks; no escort composition is written yet, so every boss brings the tier's units.

entries.name: Patrol
entries.codex: The small composition: a few foes, a fight for one machine, the threat rating its hold shows. Two stand on the flanks at the start (one from Convergence 8), and the tears send nothing else.

design.holes: The tier-one patrols read as a lone starter's fight on the greedy rung, not a tenth of its hull (docs/measurements.md, 30 October); their sizes are Ryan's to mark.

entries.name: Formation
entries.codex: The body's composition: a fight for three machines, the threat rating its hold shows. One stands on the field at the start (two from Convergence 3, three from 8), and the rift alone sends more, at its peaks. A domain's tier writes its formations; the lead's and the guest's come in turn.

design.holes: The word also names the skirmish's two ranks; the context tells them apart.

entries.name: Tear
entries.codex: A mouth beside the rift's. At a peak of Rift Pressure the ramp's count of tears (one; two from Convergence 8) open on the seam, a few rows past the rift (row 4 at twelve deep) and creeping toward the wall, as far from the rift and the other tears as the row allows, and every tear open before the peak sends a patrol. A tear opens a peak before it first sends, so where the next flood comes from is known an interval ahead. Tears stay open and never close.

design.holes: Drawn as a first cut for the phone; its mark and its opening are to judge running (RIFTGATE_PEAK_DEBUG=1 peaks every enemy turn).

entries.name: Seam
entries.codex: The flattening's edge: the row the rift's bleed reaches, a row for every five of the field's depth and one more at the start (row 4 at twelve deep), creeping two rows toward the gate at every peak, as far as the row before the wall. The tears open on it. It is the clock's picture: no rule reads the ground behind it.

design.holes: The creep a peak is a placeholder (the ramp's table, flat at two).

entries.name: Plain
entries.codex: Open ground. Every machine and pack crosses it.

entries.name: Road
entries.codex: Open ground, the same as plain: the road is art. Every machine and pack crosses it.

entries.name: Rough
entries.codex: Forest and scrub. Every machine and pack crosses it.

entries.name: Ruins
entries.codex: Rubble. Every machine and pack crosses it.

design.holes: No skirmish condition yet; what terrain does in a fight is section 12's question.

entries.name: Water
entries.codex: Tracks, walkers and wheels wade it, a hex costing two of their move; hovercraft and flyers cross it at full pace. Packs wade it as the ground machines do; a winged pack crosses it.

design.holes: No skirmish condition yet (section 12). Each map shape lays its own water (a river with fords, a fjord, ponds, a pond or none). Since 29 October the horde wades it as the ground machines do, so water slows a crossing and never walls it; the crossing guarantee binds the walls.

entries.name: Crags
entries.codex: Rock spikes. Impassable, except to flyers and winged packs.

entries.name: Mesas
entries.codex: Flat-topped rock. Impassable, except to flyers and winged packs.

entries.name: Towers
entries.codex: Dead skyscrapers. Impassable, except to flyers and winged packs.

entries.name: Cliffs
entries.codex: A wall of rock. Impassable, except to flyers and winged packs.

entries.name: Flyer
entries.codex: Crosses everything, water and walls included. It flies over machines and packs, and they pass under it, but nothing stops on another's hex.

entries.name: Hover
entries.codex: Skims water at full pace; walls stop it.

entries.name: Walker
entries.codex: Legs. Wades water at half pace.

entries.name: Tracked
entries.codex: Tracks. Wades water at half pace.

entries.name: Wheeled
entries.codex: Wheels. Wades water at half pace.

entries.name: City defense
entries.codex: A static player-side unit. Not on the field yet.

design.holes: No die and no rule yet: how gate defences work is section 12's question.

entries.name: On attack
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires on every attack, after its number is read. Effects: multiply or add damage or heat, multiply the printed number alone before any buff (the Kite's double), or set a minimum damage.

entries.name: On shield gain
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires when this machine gains shield from any source, with the amount gained; it may shed heat or grant a status, never raise more shield.

design.holes: No content uses it yet.

entries.name: On shielding an ally
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires when this machine spends a shield component on an ally, with the shield's size; it may shed the ally's heat or grant the ally a status, never raise more shield. It never fires for a shield on itself.

design.holes: Fires on the spend, whatever the shield gained, so a shield die on a topped-up ally still does its other work.

entries.name: On heat gain
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires when this machine gains heat, with the amount; it may raise shield or grant a status, never add heat.

entries.name: On round start
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires after the roll, before rerolls: shield from heat, a flat shield, a vent.

design.holes: The heat it reads is the gauge after the turn's passive cooling (the Buzzard's Thermal Recoupler).

entries.name: On skirmish start
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires once as the skirmish begins, before the first roll: a shield, a vent, a status.

design.holes: No content uses it yet.

entries.name: On foe status
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires when any foe gains a status, whoever applied it: once for each status a spend puts on a foe, however many strikes or stacks (an application, not a stack). Never for Paradox, nor for the Suppressed a Paradox causes, and Numbed is no status. Effects: paradox (the foe gains a stack of Paradox; at the count it is Suppressed and the Paradox clears).

entries.name: On applying stacks
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires when this machine applies stacks of a status to anyone: a foe's Burning (from a burn or from Primed), an ally's or its own buff, its own Empowered from a kill. Effects: add_stacks (so many stacks more, flat or for every so much heat the machine carries). Never for Numbed, which is exempt from every interaction.

design.holes: Shocked and Suppressed are not stacks, so it never touches them.

entries.name: On hull damage
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires when this machine loses hull: to a blow, a bite or an overheat.

design.holes: The hook for the pinned berserker idea too.

entries.name: On a kill
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires once after an attack of this machine's that killed, however many foes fell to it, chains, spills and a vent's blast included: a status (the Kite's Hot Streak), a shield or a vent.

entries.name: Out of combat
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires at the end of a battlefield phase in which this machine had no skirmish. Nothing may ride it: the shield is full as every fight opens, so nothing returns on the map.

design.holes: Heat does not persist between fights, so a vent here would be nothing. No content uses it yet.

entries.name: Command die
entries.codex: One die rolled alongside the machines' dice each round. Its entries are rechargeable commander abilities and never deal damage. They come from the hangar, never from rewards. Die size is a research path.

design.holes: Open question: whether the command die exists at all, or one-shots only.

entries.name: One-shot
entries.codex: Consumable ability. A pouch of three: a fourth forces a use or a discard. One comes from a Fracture's pick, and a starting stock chosen in the hangar restocks every battle. It expires when the rift closes.

entries.name: Reward pick
entries.codex: Each Fracture of the Rupture meter grants one, unweighted by domain: one of three, a battle-long modifier on a component you carry, a one-shot, or a battle-wide boon (an extra reroll a round).

design.holes: Built without one (Ryan, 24 October: maybe not warranted at all); decided after the meter is played, with the economy pass.

entries.name: City ability
entries.codex: Battlefield-level ability owned and upgraded by the city: sprint, airlift, teleport, tractor beam, orbital strike. Cooldowns measured in phases.

design.holes: Consider range limits from the gate so the push north leaves support behind.

entries.name: Tier
entries.codex: The hard scaling: a rift's tier is locked as the rift opens and sets the kind of battle: who comes, the sizes of its compositions, the Fractures to the Rupture, how many elites and which, the boss's numbers and escort. The Convergence's tier rises one every four; a rift keeps the tier it opened at, so an old rift never hardens by waiting.

design.holes: Shown on the front's card when the mission map comes; today the campaign runs headless.

entries.name: Ramp
entries.codex: The soft scaling under the tier, never shown: the Convergence as it stands when a battle starts sets how many compositions stand on the field at the start and how thick they are, how fast Rift Pressure fills, how many tears open at a peak and how far the seam creeps. It rises with the run, the same for every open front, and never resets.

design.holes: One table of placeholders (sim/ramp.gd), read by the campaign runner and moved on Ryan's word; the timer's 12 reads as the old clock's number (docs/measurements.md, 30 October).

entries.name: Cooldown
entries.codex: A cost on a component, printed along its foot as a clock and a number: once spent, its entry goes dark for that many rounds, this one included, and the die shows it dark with the clock and the turns left; the die can still land on it, and nothing in it acts. Rapid carries none of its own. No cleanse lifts a cooldown.

design.holes: A price as heat is. The city's battlefield abilities count their own cooldowns in phases.

entries.name: Reset
entries.codex: A rule printed on a weapon: if its spend kills, every entry dark from a cooldown comes back, itself included, and its machine acts again, the free roll never landing on the entry just spent; a team reroll may bring it back up, and every kill resets it again (the Kite's Pinion Driver).

design.holes: No limit (Ryan, 24 October: "Let the Kite reset infinitely. There are other ways to nerf it that aren't more rules exceptions"): the free roll never lands on the entry just spent, so each action past the second is a team reroll back onto it and another kill, and the Kite's heat climbs with every kill.

entries.name: Gather
entries.codex: A rule printed on a component (the Lammergeier's Lorentz Contractor, a debuff): every Mine the field's other foes carry joins the one its target carries, their damage added and their keywords as one.

design.holes: Ryan, 9 November: "moves all mines to a single target, and Exposes that target. The Expose rider will effectively create an AoE expose mine, which we can try and see if it's dangerous." Its Expose is its keyword, so the Mine it gathers carries Expose. A Ward on the target turns the gather away.

entries.name: Detonate
entries.codex: A rule printed on a component (the Lammergeier's Syrinx Drone, a weapon): after the spend's own Mine joins its target's, the target's Mine blows now, on it and every foe round its slot.

design.holes: Ryan, 9 November: "Deals a small amount of damage and detonates a foe's combined mine immediately ... The small chip damage makes it add a stack first. Try without a cooldown first." Its chip strike spends a Shock on the target, so a Shock doubles the chip, never the Mine.

entries.name: Sweep
entries.codex: Fires a shot at each column, left to right, repeating until it runs out of shots. It targets a rank, either one: the rank of the foe the entry is dropped on. A shot at an empty column is wasted, so a lone foe takes only its own column's shots; a foe an earlier shot felled takes its column's later shots too, since nothing is cleared until the shots are done; a massive foe fills both slots of its column, so either rank's shot there hits it. Each shot is a hit of its own, so a Shock there pops and its riders land before the next shot fires, and an area keyword's shape rides each shot. The Skua's Flechette Pod, and the Musk Ox's salvo an ammo a shot.

design.holes: Ryan, 7 November, in place of the walk of 2 and 3 November: "Fires a shot at each column, left to right, repeating until it runs out of shots"; "this makes sweep a true area mode since it will NOT stack hits on a solo boss. It also means we can make each hit more powerful without fear of it turning into a huge burst weapon", and "sweep pairs well with applying stackable debuffs". So an empty column wastes its shot and a corpse takes its column's later shots ("sweep hits a unit it already killed and doesn't skip it"). Retired: the walk that skipped empty columns so that no shot was wasted (3 November: "Empty columns at any point are skipped, so it's allowed to concentrate fire on the remainder"), since it stacked every shot on a lone foe. Still his of 2 and 3 November: a rank, either one, the shots starting at the left ("Starts left to right always"), a targeting mode of its own ("Not direct or indirect ... this means that the Skua gets indirect targeting after a fashion, and I think that's ok for its role"); in place of the spray's random darts (25 October) and the salvo's random targets (21 October), retired by the randomness pass; the HUD lights the rank under the finger whole and brackets it while a sweep is dragged.

entries.name: Regenerates
entries.codex: A rule printed on a component (the Storm Petrel's St. Elmo's Regenerator, a lure): spent on a foe, its own machine gains Regenerating, the shield it says at the start of each of the rounds it says after this one, a grant of its own each time.

design.holes: Self only and never Rapid: the die is its brake (Ryan, 19 October).

entries.name: An ally's action
entries.codex: A rule printed on a buff (the Giant Petrel's Immelmann Booster): spent on an ally whose die is spent, the team pays the rerolls it says, banked or fresh, and the ally's die rolls again, never onto the entry it showed, and it acts again. Spent on its own machine it grants what it says.

design.holes: Its price is the lever if it reads as Rapid embodied in a machine (the bible's Kestrel row); the order is the play, the ally spending first.

entries.name: Rolls its die
entries.codex: A rule printed on a buff (the Giant Petrel's Reheat Uplink): the die of the machine it lands on rolls again, never onto the entry showing. A die already spent rolls nothing.

entries.name: Rerolls a kill
entries.codex: A rule printed on a weapon (the Giant Petrel's Spindrift Salvo): if its spend kills, the team gains the rerolls it says this round, once however many fell.

entries.name: Component
entries.codex: A piece of kit on a machine, and one entry on its die. There is no generic kit: every entry on a die is a component, or an empty hardpoint. Each round the die is rolled and the component that comes up is what the machine can do.

design.holes: Multi-slot components were set aside as invisible complexity.

entries.name: Hardpoint
entries.codex: A free slot on the chassis. Any component fits any hardpoint. On the model a hardpoint is a socket where the component mounts.

entries.name: Fixed component
entries.codex: A component built into the chassis: always on the die, never removed, never sold, and it uses no hardpoint. It is the machine's own: no other machine carries one, and it can never be built.

design.holes: Never bought open. Locked pieces are powerful and unique, never blueprints, so no hardpoint stocks one and none carries a tier (the validator holds it; ContentDB.component_tier answers 0).

entries.name: Empty hardpoint
entries.codex: A hardpoint with nothing in it is an entry on the die that does nothing when it comes up. Nothing fills it for you.

entries.name: Module
entries.codex: Kit inside the machine, not on its die: a few numbers up or down, and at most one rule of its own. A chassis has its module slots (two, three on the Clydesdale), and a module is never spent: it is always working.

design.holes: Fitted in the harness and the quick campaign's hangar: the campaign's roster, the loot that drops them and its hangar wait for the economy pass and the hangar screen.

entries.name: On injury
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires when an injury lands on a component. Effects: no_destroy (the component holds instead of being destroyed).

entries.name: Armour
entries.codex: A chassis number taken off every blow that reaches the hull, flat, never a percentage: a blow on bare hull and what passes a shield alike, never a breach, which ignores it. A blow at or under the armour does nothing to the hull. Shield is not armoured: a blow on shield costs the shield its full damage.

design.holes: Numbers are placeholders.

entries.name: Strike order
entries.codex: Foes strike in the order they stand: front rank left to right, then the back rank. Each blow is resolved on its own against the shield standing at that moment, so which foe strikes first decides what a small shield blocks. At first contact the heaviest hitters deploy left.

entries.name: Aim
entries.codex: Whom a foe strikes, picked for every foe on its own as the round opens and shown as its arrow before you act: at random, unless the foe carries an aim. The foes never pile onto a machine their blows would already wreck while another stands. The exposed: weighted toward the machine its blow would hurt most, a shield standing lowering the draw and a shield about to break raising it. Anything: any machine alike. Heat: the hottest machine. The armed: a machine showing an intact weapon or debuff. Fires as one: the rank shares a pick. A move may aim differently from its foe. The pick is a commitment: a foe whose target shields up still swings at it.

design.holes: Content: aim on a foe type and on a move; when on a move is the condition that lets a foe pick it, and a special never fires twice running.

entries.name: Breach
entries.codex: A breaching blow ignores the shield and the armour: the shield stands, the armour counts for nothing, and the whole blow lands. On a foe's move it reaches a machine's hull, and if what gets through is a quarter of its maximum hull or more it destroys a component; a Ward turns it away, and the shield and armour then take the blow like any other. On a weapon it ignores a foe's armour.

entries.name: Self-Destruct
entries.codex: A blow that spends the striker: after it lands the foe is gone, whole, and nothing brings it back. The blow is the foe's whole life, so it is announced like any other and the answer is to kill it first or to shield what it has picked.

design.holes: A property of a foe's attack action, like breach. A self-destructing foe counts as a kill like any other.

entries.name: Every Machine
entries.codex: A blow at every machine: each of its strikes lands on every machine in the fight in turn, so no aim and no lure moves it, and the number shown is what each machine takes. A shield saves only the machine it stands on; the answers that stop the whole blow are aimed at the striker: kill it, suppress it, disrupt it.

design.holes: A property of a foe's attack action. Its number is per machine, so a move with it is priced well under a single blow from the same foe. The name is a working one.

entries.name: Last Act
entries.codex: A blow a foe lands the moment it falls, shown on it by the skull and its number. It lands at once, before anything else, even when the foe was the last one standing, so shield up before the kill rather than after.

design.holes: Content: on_death.blow, an attack's shape (name, factor, strikes, keywords), beside or instead of a split. The Gargantuan King's Meteor (30 October).

entries.name: Parts
entries.codex: A foe in parts: a core and the parts that stand with it. While its parts stand (all of them, or any, by the foe) the core is Guarded and takes no damage; a fallen part may grow back after a few rounds; when the core falls, its parts fall with it. Choose what to focus: a part to open the core, or the core to end them all.

design.holes: Content: parts (foe ids), guard (all or any), regrow_parts (rounds). Parts are found by pack and type, one deep, and deploy by the ordinary rules, so beside the core is likely but not placed. The Fallen Weapon's two eyes and the Obsidian Tyrant's rider (30 October); a move may open once a part has fallen (part_fallen).

entries.name: Countdown
entries.codex: A move that gathers before it lands: announced as the round opens, it lands the stated number of rounds later, its warning chip counting down the whole time. Nothing hits while it gathers. Suppress holds it a round, Disrupt breaks it off, and killing the foe ends it.

design.holes: The foe stays on the field while it gathers; its pick holds while the machine stands, and a Lure moves it.

entries.name: Follow-up
entries.codex: A move that names the move its foe announces next round. The first lands, and the second is the next round's intent, so the warning comes a round ahead: Red Capote, then Andalucia. A Suppress on the first, or a Disrupt that turns it, and the second never comes; once announced, the second cannot be Disrupted, only Suppressed.

design.holes: Content: then, on the first move, naming the second (30 October). One deep: a follow-up names none of its own and comes only after the move that names it, never by the roll. A borrowed swing with nothing taken is no follow-up, and the roll decides.

entries.name: Grudge
entries.codex: A blow that grows with the fight: a point heavier for every foe the team has killed this fight, its intent showing the number as it stands. Kill order answers it: the grudge-bearer first, the rest after.

design.holes: The Pilgrim's Karma (30 October), the Tonberry's Everyone's Grudge under a name of ours. Content: per_kill on an attack, the points a kill. Every fall counts but a foe that went whole (a burst, a part falling with its core) and one taken in by a merge.

entries.name: Foe action
entries.codex: A foe has a base attack, the quick read of how hard it hits, and a list of actions: attacks that scale it, and defends, buffs and debuffs it does instead of a blow (bracing against damage, sheltering behind a Barrier, regrowing or curing one of its own, regenerating over its next actions, cleansing the team's marks off its own, warding its side against them, readying to get back up, calling up a foe, rallying or priming the others, costing the team a reroll, setting a machine burning, silencing or purging one, switching off the entry a die shows, scorching or corrupting every machine). Each round every foe on the field picks one by weight before the player acts, so what it will do and to whom is announced exactly. An attack's damage is the base times its factor, and the help text shows the resulting number.

design.holes: A foe's whole brain is its weighted draw and its aim; none plans ahead.

entries.name: Vents all
entries.codex: An attack that fires the machine's whole heat as it is spent: the heat gauge is empty after the shot, and every step of heat fired, the step printed on the entry, adds the component's bonus to the blow before the passives. The shot's own heat cost still lands.

design.holes: Only the first shot of a chain fires the heat.

entries.name: Grows with missing HP
entries.codex: A flat blow that grows with its target's lost HP: it adds its bonus for every step of HP the target is missing, both numbers printed on the entry, read as the die is spent. No roll is involved, so the number is known before the spend, and the die shows it while held over a target.

design.holes: Both numbers are the entry's own (power_per_missing and per_missing), placeholders.

entries.name: Gated
entries.codex: A keyword printed with a condition, such as a Suppress on a foe carrying Flak or on a foe carrying two Burning or more: it lands only on a foe that meets the condition, read as the die is spent and before the blow's own riders, so a spend never opens its own gate. Held over a foe where the condition does not hold, the die shows the keyword's chip struck through.

design.holes: Suppress alone carries a gate today. A working name for Ryan's name pass.

entries.name: Consumes
entries.codex: A rule printed on a weapon: its blow consumes every stack of the status it names on its target and deals a point more for each stack consumed, before the multiplies. The die held over the foe shows the number with the stacks in.

design.holes: A mine laid from it eats its arrival's stacks.

entries.name: Burns its firer
entries.codex: A rule printed on a weapon: spending it sets its own machine Burning, the stacks it says, after the blow. The machine's Burning heats it at the end of the player's turn, before the overheat, then loses a stack, so a vent makes room for it and a cleanse takes it off. Fuel for a machine that wants heat, a price for one that does not.

design.holes: A working name for Ryan's name pass.

entries.name: The hopper
entries.codex: A rule printed on a weapon, for a machine with a hopper. One fills it: the loads it prints for each foe its blows damage, after the blow, in place of what the machine's own passive puts in. The other fires it: each load it takes adds its bonus to the blow, up to its most a shot, and the loads it takes are spent, with the Armoured they stood for. The hopper shows under the heat; the die shows what a shot would fire.

design.holes: The numbers are placeholders at the stock pass's scale.

entries.name: Braces
entries.codex: A rule printed on a component (the Breaching Plow's). Spending it Armours its owner, the stacks it says (an armour point each), until the round's end: the armour stands behind the blow through the enemy's turn.

design.holes: A rule on one carrier, not a keyword, until another piece wants it; the stacks are a placeholder.

entries.name: Rolls again
entries.codex: A rule printed on a component (the Nemesis's Knuckle of Fury). Spending it with a stack of the status it names spends one, and the die rolls again, a plain roll as the round opens, itself included, so the machine acts again and the same component may show again: the one roll again that is no reroll. Unlike Rapid nothing switches off: the stacks are the limit.

design.holes: A rule on one carrier, not a keyword, until another piece wants it.

entries.name: Strikes
entries.codex: An attack's blows per use. A weapon with three strikes lands three separate hits: each lands its own number and carries its own effects, so a rapid-fire weapon procs often; their riders land once all of them have (the Skua doubles them, its base weapon damage halved, never below one, its buffs counting on each). Against a shield, each strike is its own blow, so once one breaks the shield the next reaches the hull; against armour, every small strike loses the armour, so many small hits are the wrong tool for a heavy target and the right one for a soft one. Foe attacks have strikes too. A Sweep counts shots instead, each aimed at its own column.

design.holes: Heat is paid once per use, not per strike.

entries.name: Static
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Always on. Its effects change a machine's numbers or a component's properties while a condition holds, rather than firing on an event: add_stat and multiply_stat on hull, shield, heat, armour, move or recharge; add_damage_taken and multiply_damage_taken on every incoming blow; weapon_cooldown (every weapon the machine fires goes dark for so many rounds: the Kite's); set_reach on a component (direct or indirect while a condition holds); suppress, which turns off another effect by id or tag.

design.holes: Every read asks the pipeline; nothing is written to a stat or a component, so an effect that is gone stops answering. A static reach rule cannot be conditioned on reach.

entries.name: Order of operations
entries.codex: Everything that changes a number goes through one pipeline, in one order. Sources: the chassis passive and each fitted component's passive (until refitted), skirmish rewards (until the battle ends), buffs and debuffs (until the skirmish ends, or until the end of a given round). First suppression, shortest-lived source to longest: a live effect that suppresses another by id or tag turns it off, and a suppressed effect suppresses nothing. Then the gate: an effect takes part only if it is live, its trigger fires now, its condition holds, and, for an ability, its component is not destroyed (a destroyed component keeps its stat bonuses and loses its abilities). Then adds, all sources summed; then multiplies, all sources multiplied; then floors and caps; then overrides, where the shortest-lived source wins and the latest granted breaks ties. In an attack, the number (with what fired heat or a target's missing hull adds) comes before the pipeline's adds and multiplies; Nothing is ever stored as a total: every read asks again, so an effect that is gone stops answering. Statuses stack: the same status granted again adds stacks instead of a second copy; an add is worth its value per stack and a multiply is applied once per stack; a status that ticks applies its per-stack tick at its owner's turn, then loses one stack, and is gone at zero.

design.holes: Refit (the hangar) is what changes loadout-scoped effects; not built.

entries.name: Rage
entries.codex: Machine store, the Nemesis's: a rage for every time it takes hull damage (a blow, a bite of its own, an overheat), up to 5, kept for the skirmish. Its fists spend one when they strike, and the die rolls again. Never decays; no cleanse, Silence or Purge touches it.

design.holes: Capped at 5 (the passive's stack_status cap).

table.stacks: Yes: one a hull hit, up to 5; one spent a fist
table.lasts: The skirmish; never decays

entries.name: Hopper
entries.codex: Machine store, the Honey Badger's: every foe its weapons damage puts a load in it (its Chainsaw Claw digs two), up to four, and every two loads held are a stack of Armoured, granted as each round opens and following the loads as they come and go. Its Bullion Fragmenter fires two a shot. Lasts the skirmish; never decays, and no cleanse, Silence or Purge touches the loads: a Purge strips the Armoured they granted, until the machine's next turn.

design.holes: Its numbers since 31 October (Ryan's go, then his second fallback on the runner's read the same day): a cap of four, a point of armour for every two loads. What the loads are worth is Armoured, a buff a Purge strips, since 10 November (Ryan: "The buff he gets from it is Armoured, not an ability. Its purgeable, but returns at the start of his turn since its granted by the funnel bar"); the Ore Plate, an ability of its own, before.

table.stacks: Yes: a load a foe its weapons damage (the claw's two), up to 4; two spent a shot
table.lasts: The skirmish; never decays

entries.name: Scorched
entries.codex: Machine status, from a foe's scorch: every weapon and equipment it aims at a foe runs 1 hotter per stack, until the end of the player's turn, when every stack goes. Spending a shield, a vent, a buff or a cool weapon plays round it. Can be cleansed.

design.holes: Placeholder numbers.

table.stacks: Yes: its heat a stack
table.lasts: Until the end of the player's turn, every stack at once

entries.name: Enraged
entries.codex: Foe status, from a rage (the Goblin Nob's, its own from the fight's start). While the foe stands, every shield, vent or equipment entry the team spends lays a stack on it, and each stack is a point on every blow it lands for the rest of the fight; a weapon feeds nothing. Never spent by a move. Its chip climbs as the stacks do, so the number an intent shows is the number that lands. A Purge lowers the stacks by its number; the rage goes on, so they gather again.

design.holes: The rage's value and the Nob's numbers are placeholders. Permanent for the fight, as built (Ryan, 4 November: "Nob permanent"; Claude's lean, since an elite's job is to make the player change plan). The rage is the foe's own from the start since 8 November: it was a Bellow, the Nob's opening move, so its first round fed nothing (Ryan: "It's not innate? ... That is so unbelievably incorrect").

table.stacks: Yes: the foe's rage a non-weapon spend
table.lasts: The fight; a Purge lowers the stacks, and the rage, the Nob's Ability, goes on

entries.name: Golden
entries.codex: Foe ability, from a golden rage (the Thunder Ape's). Its blows hit its rage's value harder and it wears a point of armour for the rounds its rage says, its chip counting them down with the damage that breaks it. A quarter of its HP lost since it went gold breaks the rage and it staggers: the gold goes and it loses its next action. A Suppress breaks it too; no Purge strips it, an Ability. Calm again, it may go gold again.

design.holes: Monster Hunter's Rajang by archetype, Ryan's read of 4 November (the golden rage "is a mode, not an attack ... a cycle that forces the player into a cycle of attack and defense, broken by a bold player with great timing").
