Claude's translation: the window is the decision, shield through its rounds or burst a quarter of its HP through the extra plate to stagger it; the lost action is the bold play's pay, where the swallow's release loses none (the stun row's care; the exit if it reads as a free stun). The add is the move's value and the plate a point; numbers placeholders.

table.stacks: No: one rage at a time
table.lasts: The rage's rounds; a quarter of its HP lost since or a Suppress ends it early

entries.name: Empowered
entries.codex: Foe status, from a rally: it lands on every other foe on the field the moment the rally does, the rally's value in stacks, and every blow the foe lands hits a point harder a stack, an add before the move's factor. It halves at the end of each round, rounded down, as a machine's Empowered does: no move spends it, a Suppress takes none of it, and a foe that has acted when the rally lands carries half to the next round. Two rallies add. An intent counts the rallies on their way to it this round.

design.holes: One clock on both sides since 4 November (Ryan: "we try and make it work. If it's unbalanceable, we go back to separate keywords with different clocks"); the next-move clock of 26 October retired.

table.stacks: Yes: each rally's value adds
table.lasts: Its next move

entries.name: Undying
entries.codex: Foe status, from a Reraise, its own or an ally's. After it falls it gets back up once, whole, in its own slot and at once, unless it self-destructed; it strikes from the next round.

table.stacks: No
table.lasts: Until it falls; it returns once

entries.name: Silenced
entries.codex: Machine status, from a foe's silence: its components' keywords are muted through its next round, printed and granted alike (a Rapid entry acts once, a Spread lands one blow, its own Cleanse is a plain shield), then wake; its buffs count and its stores fill and spend as ever. Can be cleansed by an ally's Cleanse; a Ward turns the silence away.

design.holes: Its stores are untouched. Keywords alone since 28 October (buffs alone from 25 to 28 October, a one-round purge that returns); Volatile is a cost, so nothing it mutes is a price.

table.stacks: No
table.lasts: Through the machine's next round

entries.name: Swallowed
entries.codex: Machine status, from a foe's swallow. It cannot act, take damage or be targeted: a blow or a move at every machine passes it by, and no ally can shield, vent or buff it. It comes back when its rounds run out, the moment its swallower falls, or once its swallower has lost a quarter of its HP since the swallow; let go in the player's turn, it acts that round.

design.holes: Its own cooling, ticks and overheats still land, as a Phased machine's do; nothing cleanses it.

table.stacks: No
table.lasts: The swallow's rounds, or until the swallower falls or loses a quarter of its HP

entries.name: Guarded
entries.codex: Foe ability, a core's. It takes no damage while its parts stand, all of them or any, by the foe, its Burning and Vitriol included. No Purge touches it.

table.stacks: No
table.lasts: While its parts stand

entries.name: Ability
entries.codex: A unit's own mechanic, the rule it plays by: never a buff or a debuff, so no Purge, Silence or Cleanse touches it. Its chip shows its mark cut out of a solid tile: the Goblin Nob's Enrage, a core's guard, a Gel's split, a last act, the Thunder Ape's golden rage; the Polar Bear's seal, the Kite's Hot Streak.

design.holes: Ryan, 8 November, of the Nob's rage: "Nob, and any other enemies with a passive ability, should have an unpurgable passive chip that points out what's going on. Plus, that's how slay the Spire works, where he comes from. It's not a Buff, it's not a Debuff, it's labelled as an Ability, so it doesn't get purged. Can use this for player units as well, like the armadillo's form. Golden rage should be an ability chip too." The tile is a placeholder look, to judge on the phone (RIFTGATE_ABILITY_DEBUG=1).

entries.name: Barrier
entries.codex: Status, on either side. The next blow it takes deals no damage; the blow's riders land. On a machine, the next blow a foe lands on it, so it never injures, until the round's end; never granted to every ally at once. On a foe, from its own move, the next blow of a weapon the team lands on it, equipment popping nothing, until it pops or the end of the player's next turn.

table.stacks: No
table.lasts: A machine's until the next blow a foe lands on it, or the round's end; a foe's until a weapon's blow pops it, or the end of the player's next turn

entries.name: Ward
entries.codex: Status, on either side; a blow's damage lands. On a machine, no rider a foe lays lands on it this round, from a blow or from a move of its own (breach, burn, scorch, disable, corrupt, silence, purge), until the round's end. On a foe, from a move that wards every foe on the field, no mark the team lays lands on it (Burning, Flak, Cryo, Vitriol, Shocked, Exposed, Webbed, the Paradox and the drone), nor a stun, nor a Purge, and a turned mark feeds no Paradox, until the end of the player's next turn.

design.holes: A foe's move that lays a debuff without a blow is a rider too (Ryan, 25 October: "Should stop all riders, even from non-damaging attacks"), so a Stoke, a Stone, an Eruption on every machine and a Diamond Dust all pass a warded machine by. A foe's Ward (28 October) turns the team's marks (Effects.TEAM_MARKS), and since 2 November a stun and a Purge too, on either side, and stands (Ryan: nothing but damage lands on a Warded foe; the exception that let a stun through went with Numbed's roll).

table.stacks: No
table.lasts: A machine's the round; a foe's until the end of the player's next turn

entries.name: Scorch
entries.codex: Foe attack keyword with a number. Each blow that lands leaves that many stacks of Scorched on the machine it hit (Scorch 2: two): every weapon and equipment it aims at a foe runs hotter.

entries.name: Crush
entries.codex: Foe attack keyword with a number. Each blow that lands leaves that many stacks of Crushed on the machine it hit (Crush 2: two): every blow it takes through the next round deals a point more a stack. A Ward turns it away; an ally's Cleanse lifts the mark.

design.holes: The World Eater's pin (4 November); see Crushed.

entries.name: Menace
entries.codex: A foe's weight: its heaviest blow plus a quarter of its HP, rounded up; an elite's doubled. The Rupture meter, Anathema and salvage count every kill by it, so the rift's reinforcements pay a trickle and the field's formations and the elites pay the most.

design.holes: The formula is Claude's placeholder, one weight for the three tallies; the bosses' menace counts as any foe's.

entries.name: Elite
entries.codex: A unique foe leading its own composition, worth double its menace, emerging at the rift at a Fracture. Each tier names which Fractures bring one; the lead domain's elites come in turn and never twice in a battle, or a wanderer, drawn on the Fracture's roll one time in three and always once the domain's own are spent. An elite stands at the battle's tier as a boss does.

design.holes: Five placeholder kits (the goblin shaman, the Elder Treant, the Leshy, the Old Man of the Desert, the Reaper) for Ryan's marks; the Peak's elite and a Waste hunter wait on them; the Bone Wyvern waits on the slate.

entries.name: Seal
entries.codex: The boss's seal holds until the Rupture: while it does the boss cannot be attacked and joins no fight, its ring inert, SEALED on its readout. The Rupture breaks it, by the last Fracture or by a cleared field.

design.holes: The seal's look on the ring is a first cut for the phone.

entries.name: Muster
entries.codex: Machine store, the Swallowtail's: a charge its locked pieces spend for their charged forms. Every die that rolls fills it a sliver, about thirty rolls a charge, and a kill by its own guns five rolls' worth; stored up to its cap. Starts each fight empty and never decays; a store, so no Silence or Purge touches it. With a charge up, its locked pieces go out charged unasked, unless the charged form has nowhere to land; then the plain form goes out and the charge waits.

design.holes: Every number is a placeholder; carrying it between fights is section 12's heat question.

table.stacks: Yes: a charge about thirty rolls of any die, five rolls' worth a kill by its guns, up to its cap
table.lasts: The skirmish; never decays

entries.name: Rallied
entries.codex: Machine status, the Swallowtail's Reveille Horn: its team has one reroll more this round.

design.holes: The reroll it grants counts toward the Muster when spent on the carrier: the intended combo, held by the cap.

table.stacks: No
table.lasts: The round

entries.name: Charged
entries.codex: Machine buff. While it lasts the machine's weapons fire with Shock, shown on the die: every foe a fire reaches is Shocked after the blows, a felled one too. A weapon fired spends a stack: a Rapid's second fire is a second fire, a salvo one, a blast none, and equipment carries it not and spends nothing. A laid shot spends the stack as it is laid and carries the Shock. A Purge lowers it.

design.holes: The Shock primer (Ryan, 2 November), Primed's cousin, so Chain is the arcs alone and the Shock supply is a kit choice; a keyword on the weapon fired, never a mark per hit (3 November: "a multi-hit weapon with Shock would apply it after both hits"), so a strikes gun never cashes what it just laid. No piece grants it yet: capacitor pieces are content to propose.

table.stacks: Yes: a fire spends one
table.lasts: Until spent

entries.name: Supercooled
entries.codex: Machine buff. While it lasts the machine's weapons fire with Cryo, one more stack a strike on each foe hit (Cryo 1 on a gun without it), shown on the die and laid after the hits, so a fire never cashes its own frost. A weapon fired spends a stack: a Rapid's second fire is a second fire, a salvo one, a blast none, and equipment carries it not and spends nothing. A laid shot spends the stack as it is laid and carries the frost. A Purge lowers it.

design.holes: The Cryo primer (Ryan, 2 November: "laying 1 cryo at a time makes sense, keeps it a little unique, and avoids massive cooling spikes"; the name his pick), so any gun is a Cryo setter for a turn and the Cryo synergies open past the Cryo Flinger; a stack a strike after the hits (3 November: "resulting in 2 applications, not apply-cash-apply-cash, and not hit-hit-apply once"). No piece grants it yet.

table.stacks: Yes: a fire spends one
table.lasts: Until spent

entries.name: Regenerating
entries.codex: Status, on either side. A foe's, from its own move: it regrows its value in HP at each of its next three actions, after its Burning and Vitriol have ticked, so a burn is a race and never a wall. A machine's, from the Storm Petrel's St. Elmo's Regenerator: it regains its value in shield at the start of each of the next three rounds, up to its maximum. Each grant keeps its own clock, so two add until the first runs out.

design.holes: The machine half, the Storm Petrel's, built 30 October: a timed grant of its own each spend, the shield at each round's start after it, bought by a die entry so a foe's purge takes it. The numbers are placeholders.

table.stacks: Yes: each grant its own clock
table.lasts: A foe's three of its actions; a machine's three rounds from its grant

entries.name: Ammo
entries.codex: The Musk Ox's magazine, a bar under its heat bar, a notch an ammo. Its weapons spend ammo instead of heating it: 1 for every 2 heat a gun would make, rounded up, at least 1, the price printed where the gun's heat would be; a foe's Scorched still heats them. The magazine holds 10, opens each fight at 3 and gains 1 at the start of every round after the first; a vent the Musk Ox spends on itself adds 3, a shield 2. With too little left, a gun cannot be spent (DRY).

design.holes: Never a buff, so no Silence or Purge reaches it. If ammo runs plentiful, the vents' and shields' reloads or the trickle come down.
